title: Reference Terraform modules for App Connectors on GCP
aliases: gcp app connector managed instance group

prose.text: The GCP reference modules deploy App Connector VMs as zonal managed instance groups behind a Cloud NAT and create the ZPA App Connector Group and Provisioning Key. They are the GCP counterpart of the AWS and Azure modules described in [[zpa.app-connectors.deployment]].

prose.label: Image and bootstrap.
prose.text: {{image-pinned}} {{image-rhel9-fallback}} {{bootstrap-provision-key}} {{group-user-codes}} How the user codes are collected is open {{gap:oauth-flow-on-gcp}}; see [[zpa.app-connectors.enrollment]].

checks.do: Which VM size and disk the module deploys.
Whether the deployment is fixed-size or autoscaling and what the min and max apply to (per zone).
Whether the provisioning key max_usage leaves headroom for scale-out and replacement.
What the autohealing health check actually probes.
Which version profile the module-created group ends up with.

rhel9-since-1-1-0.statement: As of module version 1.1.0 the GCP App Connector module deploys all App Connectors on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.

quotes: As of version 1.1.0 of this module, all App Connectors are deployed using the new [Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9]

provider-versions.statement: The README lists the Google provider v7.31.x, random v3.8.x, local v2.8.x, null v3.2.x, tls v4.2.x and the ZPA provider v4.4.x, with Terraform v1.1.9 and any Terraform version 0.13.7 generally supported.

quotes: The GCP Terraform scripts leverage Terraform v1.1.9
any Terraform version 0.13.7 should be generally supported.

oneapi-auth.statement: The module authenticates the ZPA provider through OneAPI (OAuth2 via Zidentity), which the README recommends for new deployments; the provider keeps the legacy ZPA API framework for tenants not yet migrated, and OneAPI and Zidentity are not supported in the GOV and GOVUS clouds.

quotes: authenticates against Zscaler [OneAPI](https://help.zscaler.com/oneapi/understanding-oneapi) using OAuth2 through [Zidentity](https://help.zscaler.com/zidentity/what-zidentity). OneAPI is the recommended authentication method for all new deployments.
The provider also retains backwards compatibility with the legacy ZPA API framework for organizations whose tenants have not yet been migrated to Zidentity.
**NOTE:** OneAPI and Zidentity are not supported in the `GOV` and `GOVUS` clouds. Tenants in those environments must use the legacy ZPA authentication method.

gcp-prereqs.statement: The examples need a GCP project with billing enabled and the compute.googleapis.com, iam.googleapis.com and cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com APIs enabled; authentication is Application Default Credentials (recommended) or a service account keyfile with at least roles/compute.admin and roles/iam.serviceAccountUser.

quotes: Recommended: Application Default Credentials (`gcloud auth application-default login`). Leave the `credentials` tfvar commented out.
Or: a service account JSON keyfile with at least `roles/compute.admin` and `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser`.

example-types.statement: The GCP module ships four examples: base_ac and base_ac_asg (greenfield, with a Management VPC, Cloud Router, NAT and a bastion host) and ac and ac_asg (brownfield, no bastion, every network primitive reusable through byo_* variables); the base_ac and ac examples run a fixed ac_count per zone and the _asg examples add a Compute Autoscaler per zone.

quotes: Fixed (`base_ac` / `ac`)** examples deploy a pinned number of App Connectors per zone (`ac_count`).
Autoscaling (`base_ac_asg` / `ac_asg`)** examples add a `google_compute_autoscaler` per zonal MIG
Every network primitive is byo_* togglable
(VPC, subnet, Cloud Router, NAT). No bastion. Use for production with a steady-state connector count.
1 new Management VPC + AC subnet + bastion subnet, 1 Cloud Router + NAT,
Same brownfield BYO surface as ac (no bastion,
1 bastion host with auto-generated SSH key pair

vm-size.statement: The GCP App Connector VM module defaults acvm_instance_type to n2-standard-4 and validates it against n2-standard-4, n2-highcpu-4, n1-standard-4, n1-highcpu-4, n2-standard-8, n2-highcpu-8, n1-standard-8 and n1-highcpu-8.

vm-template.statement: Each App Connector instance template boots from a pd-balanced boot disk whose size defaults to 64 GB, with automatic_restart true and on_host_maintenance MIGRATE.

fixed-mig-layout.statement: The fixed-size module creates one zonal managed instance group per zone, each with target_size equal to ac_count (default 1), so total connectors are ac_count times the number of zones.

quotes: # Create Zonal Managed Instance Groups per number of zones defined
# Create X number of App Connectors in each group per ac_count variable

zones-az-count.statement: The examples create zonal groups in the first az_count available zones of the region (az_count defaults to 1 and is validated between 1 and 3), or in the distinct zones listed in the zones variable when it is non-empty.

update-policy.statement: The MIG update policy defaults to type OPPORTUNISTIC, replacement method SUBSTITUTE, maximum surge 1 and maximum unavailable 1, with minimal and most-disruptive action REPLACE; per the variable description OPPORTUNISTIC means no action is proactively executed and an update happens as part of other actions such as resizes or recreateInstances calls.

quotes: OPPORTUNISTIC so that no action is proactively executed but the update will be performed as part of other actions (for example, resizes or recreateInstances calls)

image-pinned.statement: The examples look up a specific named image, zpa-connector-el9-2025-11, in the Google Marketplace project mpi-zpa-gcp-marketplace when use_zscaler_image is true (the default), although the image_name variable description says templates always pull the latest from Google Marketplace.

quotes: Ideally all VMs should be on the same Image as templates always pull the latest from Google Marketplace.
Custom image name to be used for deploying App Connector appliances.

image-rhel9-fallback.statement: With use_zscaler_image false the examples use the latest rhel-9 family image from the rhel-cloud project and a startup script that writes the Zscaler yum repository https://yum.private.zscaler.com/yum/el9 and installs zpa-connector.

bootstrap-provision-key.statement: The example startup scripts stop the zpa-connector service, write the Terraform-managed provisioning key to /opt/zscaler/var/provision_key, run yum update -y, start zpa-connector, sleep 60 and restart it.

quotes: systemctl stop zpa-connector systemctl start zpa-connector

group-user-codes.statement: The GCP App Connector group module declares user_codes (default an empty list), described as OAuth2 user codes retrieved from the deployed VMs' /etc/issue for enrolling with the OAuth2 method, and passes them to the zpa_app_connector_group resource.

quotes: OAuth2 user codes retrieved from deployed App Connector VMs (/etc/issue). These codes are required for enrolling App Connectors using the new OAuth2 authentication method.

group-fixed-lookups.statement: The group module hardcodes the enrollment certificate lookup to the name Connector and pins version_profile_id to the id of the customer version profile named Default, neither exposed as a variable.

quotes: certificate name is intentionally hardcoded and not exposed as a variable.
so the profile name is intentionally hardcoded and not exposed as a variable.

group-defaults.statement: The GCP group module defaults upgrade_day to SUNDAY, upgrade_time_in_secs to 66600 (a string, valid from 0 to under 86400 in 15 minute intervals) and dns_query_type to IPV4_IPV6, validated against IPV4_IPV6, IPV4 and IPV6.

quotes: The integer should be greater than or equal to 0 and less than 86400, in 15 minute intervals

key-module.statement: The provisioning key module hardcodes the Connector enrollment certificate, accepts only association type CONNECTOR_GRP, binds the key to the group through zcomponent_id, and with byo_provisioning_key true creates no key and only references an existing one by name.

quotes: # Retrieve the "Connector" enrollment certificate used to sign App Connector
# "Connector", so the certificate name is intentionally hardcoded and not
Setting this variable to true will effectively instruct this module to not create any resources and only reference data resources from values provided in byo_provisioning_key_name

key-max-usage.statement: The provisioning key max_usage defaults to 10 in the fixed examples and 100 in the autoscaling examples; each App Connector consumes one slot at enrollment and instance churn (image upgrades, scale-in and scale-out, MIG replacements) consumes more, and when the key runs out new VMs come up healthy at the OS level but show as disconnected in the ZPA portal.

quotes: Each App Connector consumes one slot at enrollment time and instance churn (image upgrades, scale-in/out, MIG replacements) consumes additional slots even though the old VMs are gone.
running out causes new VMs to come up healthy at the OS level but show as disconnected in the ZPA portal.

asg-defaults.statement: The autoscaling module defaults min_size to 2 and max_size to 4, both per zone, with target_cpu_util_value 50, cooldown_period 60 seconds and health_check_grace_period 300 seconds.

quotes: Minimum number of App Connectors to maintain in the autoscaling group (per zone)
Maximum number of App Connectors to maintain in the autoscaling group (per zone)

variable "cooldown_period" { type = number description = "The number of seconds the autoscaler waits before it starts collecting information from a new instance. Prevents the autoscaler from acting on usage data while the instance is still initializing." default     = 60

variable "health_check_grace_period" { type = number description = "Time in seconds the autohealing health check waits before checking a newly created instance. Mirrors AWS health_check_grace_period semantics." default     = 300

asg-metrics.statement: The autoscaling module accepts target_tracking_metric ASGAverageCPUUtilization (the default and the recommended one), ASGAverageNetworkIn or ASGAverageNetworkOut; the CPU target is a percentage divided by 100 internally, and for the network metrics the same target_cpu_util_value is read as bytes per second per instance.

quotes: divided by 100 internally because GCP wants a 0.0-1.0 fraction

asg-health-check.statement: Autoscaling-group autohealing uses a TCP health check on port 22 (timeout 5 seconds, interval 10 seconds, healthy threshold 2, unhealthy threshold 3) with initial_delay_sec equal to health_check_grace_period, because the module's comment says the App Connector listens on no externally-routable port.

quotes: The App Connector listens on no
externally-routable port (it dials out to the Zscaler cloud), so we use a
basic TCP check on the SSH port.

asg-owns-size.statement: In the autoscaling module the autoscaler owns the group size: target_size is left unset on each MIG and ignored in lifecycle changes so Terraform does not fight the autoscaler, and one MIG plus one autoscaler is created per zone.

quotes: target_size is intentionally left unset so the
autoscaler is the sole authority on group size.
# Once the autoscaler attaches, target_size is owned by it.

network-resources.statement: The network module creates a custom-mode VPC (auto_create_subnetworks false, routing_mode REGIONAL by default), one App Connector subnet, a Cloud Router and a Cloud NAT gateway with AUTO_ONLY address allocation for all subnetworks and ERRORS_ONLY logging; each of VPC, subnet, router and NAT can instead be referenced with byo_* variables.

quotes: # Or reference an existing NAT Gateway
Every network primitive is byo_* togglable
(VPC, subnet, Cloud Router, NAT). No bastion.

network-firewall.statement: The module's management firewall allows tcp on allowed_ports (an empty default list means all ports) and icmp (icmpv6 in the IPv6 rule) only from allowed_ssh_from_internal_cidr, split into an IPv4 rule and an IPv6 rule because GCP firewall rules cannot mix address families; the examples set that source list to the bastion subnet CIDR.

quotes: GCP firewall rules cannot mix IPv4 and IPv6 source_ranges in a single rule
A list of ports to permit inbound to App Connector. Default empty list means to allow all.

bastion-open.statement: In the greenfield examples the bastion host gets an ephemeral public IP and firewall rules allowing tcp/22 from bastion_ssh_allow_ip (IPv4 and IPv6 ranges in separate rules), which defaults to 0.0.0.0/0.

quotes: Permit SSH access to bastion host from approved IPv4 source ranges
Permit SSH access to bastion host from approved IPv6 source ranges

name-prefix.statement: The examples validate name_prefix to 12 or fewer characters matching ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]+$, with default zsac.

destroy-removes-zpa.statement: Destroying an example removes the App Connectors and also the ZPA App Connector Group and Provisioning Key; access policies that reference the group must be detached first or the destroy fails on the ZPA side.

quotes: destroy removes the App Connectors *and* the ZPA App Connector Group and Provisioning Key. If you have ZPA access policies referencing the group, detach them first or the destroy will fail on the ZPA side.

wrapper-auth.statement: The examples/zsac wrapper script supports ZPA provider authentication through OneAPI/Zidentity (ZSCALER_CLIENT_ID, ZSCALER_CLIENT_SECRET, ZSCALER_VANITY_DOMAIN) or the legacy ZPA framework (ZPA_CLIENT_ID, ZPA_CLIENT_SECRET, ZPA_CUSTOMER_ID, ZPA_CLOUD with ZSCALER_USE_LEGACY_CLIENT=true), the latter for tenants still on the legacy framework or GOV/GOVUS.

quotes: Legacy ZPA (for tenants still on the legacy framework, or GOV/GOVUS)
env vars: ZPA_CLIENT_ID, ZPA_CLIENT_SECRET, ZPA_CUSTOMER_ID, ZPA_CLOUD,

wrapper-script-name.summary: What the interactive wrapper script is called.

positions.says: The README calls the wrapper zsac.

quotes: If executing Terraform via the `zsac` wrapper bash script

positions.says: The examples README documents it as zsec, with a .zsecrc cache.

quotes: The `zsec` script is intended for first-time operators
Validates inputs and writes a .zsecrc cache for subsequent runs

positions.says: The script file itself is examples/zsac, with the usage line ./zsac and a .zsacrc cache.

wrapper-script-name.impact: Commands copied from the examples README (./zsec up, ./zsec destroy, deleting .zsecrc) do not match the script that ships; use ./zsac and .zsacrc.

override-version-profile-default.summary: Whether the group module overrides the version profile by default.

positions.says: The variable description says the default is false.

quotes: Whether the default version profile of the App Connector Group is applied or overridden. Default: false

override-version-profile-default.impact: A group created with the module defaults has override_version_profile true and a version_profile_id pinned to the profile named Default, not the false the description implies; confirm the group in the ZPA Admin Portal before assuming it follows the tenant default.

oauth-flow-on-gcp.title: OAuth2 user-code enrollment on GCP
oauth-flow-on-gcp.detail: The group module accepts user_codes read from /etc/issue on the VMs, but the examples bootstrap with a provisioning key written to a file; the repository does not describe how an operator collects the user codes from MIG-managed VMs and applies them.
